intended_object: The ghost-sample measure from the symmetrization argument in learning theory: for a distribution D on X and a sample size m, the law of an i.i.d. sample S ~ Dᵐ together with an independent ghost sample S′ ~ Dᵐ, i.e. Dᵐ ⊗ Dᵐ on Xᵐ × Xᵐ. Inferred from the docstring ("Product measure on a pair of independent ghost samples") and the name.
explanation: The body is `(Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin m => D)).prod (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin m => D))`, which is exactly the product of the m-fold product measure Dᵐ with itself on `(Fin m → X) × (Fin m → X)`. Because it is a product measure, the two samples are independent. Because `Measure.pi` is a product of identical factors, the coordinates within each sample are i.i.d. When m = 0 the result is the Dirac mass on the pair of empty samples, which is the correct degenerate value. X is an arbitrary measurable space and D an arbitrary measure, so the definition is as general as it can be. Indexing samples by `Fin m` is the standard way to represent a sample of size m, so it does not make the definition too narrow. Mathlib has no named ghost-sample measure; the definition is a direct combination of `Measure.pi` and `Measure.prod`.
